newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to take look at Asian rice prices - trade.
newsitem.headline: Manila to take look at Asian rice prices - trade.

text.p: The Philippines will probably begin looking at Asian rice prices next week ahead of its plan to import up to 650,000 tonnes of rice to beef up reserves before July 1997, traders said on Friday.
"The play on the Philippine commodities market next week will centre on the National Food Authority's rice importation," a senior trader in a U.S.-based commodities house said.

NFA assistant administrator Vic Racho told Reuters on Thursday his agency would shortly review a rice offer from Vietnam after the NFA received approval from President Fidel Ramos to import about 650,000 tonnes of the staple before the
Racho said Philippine rice stocks stood at 1.8 million tonnes at the start of February this year, of which around 300,000 tonnes were in NFA warehouses.
The Philippines consumes an average of 22,000 tonnes of rice per day, he added.
An official from the Agriculture Department said last month he expected the country's buffer rice stocks to fall below the ideal 90-day level, or around 860,000 tonnes, before the beginning of July.
Traders from Pakistan, India and China have also offered to supply the rice requirement of the Philippines, he said.
The NFA has so far bought 55,000 tonnes of Thai rice for delivery in March and April.
"Under the same agreement, we have an option to buy an additional 150,000 tonnes of rice from Thailand," Racho said.
Manila traders said Vietnam has offered to sell rice to the Philippines at a cheaper price, or US$5 to $10 lower than the $300 per tonne price of the Thai rice bought recently.
The government has set 1.98 million tonnes, or stocks sufficient for three months, as an ideal cushion to maintain to ensure there would be no shortages in the country.
On the other hand, local wheat and corn importers will likely stay away from the market because of high prices, dealers said.
"But as to wheat I don't expect any orders due to prospects that U.S. wheat would rise further next week," a trader said.
In the corn market, poultry and livestock farmers awaited the delivery next week of 100,000 tonnes of Chinese corn bought by the NFA last month, traders said.
Traders said prices of local flour remained steady, with the price of a 25-kg bag of hard flour pegged at 290 pesos while the same quantity of soft flour was quoted at 260 pesos.

The NFA said the retail price of a kg of yellow corn was steady at 10.56 pesos while white corn was quoted at 11.03 a kg. The farm gate price of white corn dropped to 6.87 pesos per kg from 6.89 pesos while a kg of yellow corn softened to 6.82 pesos from 6.87 pesos.
